text: Lineage isn't bookkeeping for its own sake. This lesson covers four concrete business reasons organizations invest in it, and what actually breaks, in practical terms, when it doesn't exist.

Trust — when a number looks wrong, lineage answers where it came from instead of 'nobody fully knows.' Impact analysis — before changing a column, you know exactly what downstream reports depend on it. Root cause analysis — you walk backward to the exact hop where things diverged. Audit requirements — regulated industries need to prove how a figure was calculated, from source to final number.

Picture a revenue number that drops unexpectedly. Without lineage, three people independently check three systems, duplicating effort, because nobody has a map of what feeds that number. With lineage, the team opens the record, sees every hop, and checks each one in order. The investigation becomes mechanical instead of exploratory.

Metadata Management closed on giving every concept one definition and one home. Lineage extends that from identity to movement — proving every report pulling that concept is pulling it correctly, through every hop, rather than silently drifting onto a stale copy somewhere else.
Next up: business lineage versus technical lineage — the difference between a readable summary for stakeholders and the detailed map engineers actually use to debug.
